usageNotes: Use this to change a PVE user's password; each user may change their own password, or an admin with Realm.AllocateUser + User.Modify on a shared group can change another user's password. API tokens are not accepted (allowtoken: false), so the caller must authenticate with a full user session or ticket. For PAM realm users, the change only applies to the local node — not cluster-wide.

examples.summary: Admin resets password for a local PVE user

tips: allowtoken is false — API token auth will be rejected; use a user ticket (POST /access/ticket) instead.
PAM realm password changes are node-local only; for cluster-wide effect the underlying Linux account must be synced externally.
The confirmation-password field is required when a non-admin user changes their own password to confirm current credentials; admins changing another user's password typically omit it.
Passwords must be 8–64 characters; enforce complexity at the application layer since the API only validates length.
Returns null on success — treat any non-2xx response as failure.
